solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Anxiety around heath, nothing less

parts.note: angst is a German-derived word for dread or anxiety

indicators.note: around signals that the trimmed heath word is turned round and read backwards
less tells us the nothing letter is taken away from the heath word

parts.note: a moor is open heathland
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone troubled by worry about open countryside, without any mitigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the heath word only after 'less' has removed its O. The clue gives no definition: the answer is one of the puzzle's themed units of measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of length of one ten-billionth of a metre, used for atomic distances, fitting the measurement theme.

clue.text: Holy man coming from Le Mans

indicators.note: coming from suggests the letters are produced out of the town's name by reworking them

explanation.surface: A saint arriving from the French town of motor-racing fame.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog finds no clear anagram signal; 'coming from' is the nearest.
explanation.definitionFit: St Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury, was a saint and theologian.

clue.text: Country house's grand spread

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
a range is a spread, as of prices

explanation.surface: A rural mansion with an impressive layout.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings attached.

clue.text: Stigma, albeit isn't common

parts.note: albeit carries the sense 'though it', supplying the clipped 'T for it
ain't is the vulgar, common form of isn't

explanation.surface: Acknowledging a social stigma that is, however, rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T AIN'T is dialect for 'it isn't'; one commenter complained that 'isn't' alone should mean 'it isn't'.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a mark of disgrace or a stain on a reputation.

clue.text: Batsmen 1 and 2 in key roles

definitions.meaning: in cricket the first two batters in the order start the innings
keys are tools for unlocking doors

explanation.surface: Praise for the top two batters' vital part in the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening batsmen start a cricket innings, and things that unlock doors, like keys, do this job.

clue.text: Sound, you understand

definitions.meaning: to sound water is to measure its depth
to grasp or comprehend something, as in 'I can't work it out'

explanation.surface: A speaker checking that the listener has followed them.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to measure depth with a line and to comprehend, and the noun is a six-foot unit of depth.

clue.text: Unaccompanied singing in palace — and lap dancing!

indicators.note: dancing letters jig about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Choral music in a royal residence, alongside a racy floor show.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for 'in chapel style', it means voices without instrumental backing.

clue.text: Fun having vermouth during Oxford term

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the span of the other

parts.note: Hilary is the spring term at Oxford University
IT is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A student drinking vermouth and having a good time at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is merriment or loud amusement, much the same as fun.

clue.text: Artist in German capital filling his face

parts.note: Edvard Munch, Norwegian painter of The Scream

indicators.note: a capital is an upper-case first letter, so take the opening letter of German

explanation.surface: A painter in Berlin eating greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' looks like Berlin, but it is just the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill one's face is to eat heartily, which is chewing food noisily.

clue.text: Sesame oil spilt — nothing lost

indicators.note: spilt oil runs everywhere, so these letters are thrown into a new order
lost says the nothing letter goes missing from the pool before rearranging

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A kitchen accident with cooking oil where, luckily, none was wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: SESAME OIL without one O leaves SESAMEIL, rearranged by 'spilt'. There is no definition: the answer is one of the themed units.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical units of distance, each about 1,852 metres, belonging to the measurement theme of the grid.

clue.text: Capacity of old vessel reduced by one quarter

indicators.note: reduced by says the ship's name loses a letter

parts.note: a galleon is an old sailing ship
east is one of the four quarters of the compass, E

explanation.surface: How much an antique ship could hold after a quarter was lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One quarter' looks like a fraction, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of liquid volume, eight pints, is a measure of capacity.

clue.text: Viking Red explorer, terribly heartsick but chats away

indicators.note: terribly signals the remaining letters come out in a jumbled order
chats away means the letters of chats are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A homesick Norse explorer chatting to ease his longing.
explanation.walkthrough: HEARTSICK less C, H, A, T, S leaves ERIK, in the order 'terribly' shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik the Red was the Norse explorer who founded the first settlement in Greenland.

clue.text: Land on time from long distance

parts.note: to light on or alight is to land, as a bird does
a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: An aircraft arriving on schedule after a very long flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The astronomical unit is the distance light travels in a year, a vast span.

clue.text: A creature caught with a rod — a rod

definitions.text: A creature caught with a rod
definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish taken by anglers
an old unit of length of five and a half yards, also called a pole

explanation.surface: An angler's catch described twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the freshwater fish and the old length measure, equal to a pole, share this name.

clue.text: Cloth to dispose of first to last

definitions.note: the answer is plural, measures used for cloth; the clue gives the material they measure

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter is shifted to the end

parts.note: to sell goods is to dispose of them

explanation.surface: Instructions for clearing out fabric stock.
explanation.walkthrough: An ell was an old measure of cloth, about 45 inches, so the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Old English lengths, each about 45 inches, used chiefly for measuring fabric.

clue.text: Merkel's description of broken reed in unproductive bit of enterprise

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the unproductive word

parts.note: lean means unfruitful, as in lean years

indicators.note: broken letters are smashed apart and reassembled
bit of takes just a small piece, the first letter

explanation.surface: Political commentary on a weak patch of a German business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the reed letters before 'in' sets them within the unproductive word. The coinage was first used of Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular term for a dominant female leader, coined for Thatcher, applies to Angela Merkel.

clue.text: A lot of explosive too unstable in oven

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the oven word

parts.note: a kiln is an oven for firing pottery

indicators.note: unstable letters do not hold their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that something dangerously volatile is in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unstable' rearranges the word too before 'in' places it in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of explosive power equal to a thousand tons of TNT, so a large amount.

clue.text: Voted to assign shares in plot

indicators.note: in puts the sharing word inside the plot word

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
to allot is to share out

explanation.surface: A conspiracy where members voted to divide the spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: To ballot is to vote secretly, so the past tense matches voted.

clue.text: Worrying about ornamenting

definitions.meaning: decorating with fretwork or carved patterns

explanation.surface: Anxious over decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to worry, and also to decorate with interlaced patterns.

clue.text: Area about to be bordered by a goal

indicators.note: to be bordered by puts one piece within the edges of another

parts.note: in ice hockey the goal is called the cage
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A pitch description: the space round a goalmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' is the ice hockey sense, the netted cage; 'to be bordered by' puts the about word within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is land area measured in acres, an extent of ground.

clue.text: Expert returns to exile location

indicators.note: returns means the word comes back the other way

parts.note: an able person is skilled or expert

explanation.surface: A specialist going back to where someone was banished.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was banished to this Mediterranean island in 1814.

clue.text: Fish caught and smuggled

definitions.note: the answer is a measure of fresh herrings, so the clue's fish stands for it loosely

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to run contraband is to smuggle it

explanation.surface: Contraband seafood seized by customs.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Scottish measure of fresh herrings, about 37.5 gallons, is a quantity of fish.

clue.text: Bowling during series creates storm in Sri Lanka

indicators.note: during sets one piece inside the other

parts.note: a cycle is a series of events
a bowler who is on is currently bowling in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket tour where bowling conditions are wrecked by bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian Ocean name for a tropical revolving storm, the hurricane's counterpart.

clue.text: President no longer — disgusting toerag?

definitions.note: Daniel Ortega of Nicaragua, a former president (he later returned to office)

indicators.note: disgusting suggests something gone bad, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An insulted ex-leader called a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: A toerag is British slang for a rogue. Ortega was in fact back in office when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Ortega led Nicaragua in the 1980s, an ex-head of state.

clue.text: Santa likely, initially, to move cautiously on it?

definitions.text: Santa likely, initially, to move cautiously on it?

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: to edge forward is to move slowly and carefully

explanation.surface: Wondering what Father Christmas rides as he inches along.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa travels by sleigh, a vehicle on runners for snow.

clue.text: Left Italian red, not finishing contents of carafe?

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, as in gin and it

indicators.note: not finishing means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A wine order: left some Italian red, not drinking it all.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a carafe's contents are only sometimes this volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe of wine typically holds about this metric unit of volume.

clue.text: German tennis player suggested Nadal's article

definitions.text: German tennis player suggested Nadal's article

indicators.note: suggested means the first part only resembles the player's name in speech

parts.note: Boris Becker, German Wimbledon champion
Rafael Nadal is Spanish, and el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Tennis gossip: a German star's remark about a piece written by Nadal.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no definition: the answer is one of the puzzle's units, the SI unit of radioactivity.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of radioactivity, one decay per second, named after Henri Becquerel.

clue.text: Disconcerted — but following increase, hardened

indicators.note: following puts the hardened word after the increase word

parts.note: to up a price is to increase it
concrete that has set has hardened

explanation.surface: Someone flustered by a pay rise yet steeled against it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be upset is to be troubled or thrown off balance.

clue.text: Lengths to which they move slowly when placed on high ground

indicators.note: the answer, when placed after the high ground word, makes the slow movers; so take that word away

parts.note: tortoises are proverbially slow
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how far slow creatures travel on a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR followed by the answer spells TORTOISES. A toise is an old French length of about two metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Old French units of length, each roughly two metres, so measures of distance.

clue.text: Monopolises the principal

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it all to oneself
a head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: A complaint that the headteacher keeps everything for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has no definition: the answer is one of the themed units, a large cask. The grid printed HOGSGEAD, a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cask and a liquid measure of around 52 imperial gallons, part of the units theme.

clue.text: To an extent, it denotes education

definitions.meaning: a university qualification shows study completed

explanation.surface: A remark that qualifications only partly signal learning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a level or extent, and also an academic award showing schooling achieved.

clue.text: Meg left corrupt race meeting

indicators.note: corrupt letters are spoilt and jumbled into a fresh order
left means the name Meg is gone from the pool of letters

explanation.surface: A woman named Meg walks out of a crooked day at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: RACE MEETING without M, E, G leaves RACEETIN, rearranged by 'corrupt'. There is no definition: it is a themed unit, a hundredth of an are.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of area, one square metre, belonging to the measurement theme.
